episodes.157823: A small MCS crossed the Laurel Highlands during the late morning hours of June 13, 2021, with wind damage being reported in Somerset County. Later in the day, additional showers and storms developed in the very warm and humid airmass over central Pennsylvania, ahead of an approaching cold front. These late-day storms produced sporadic wind damage and hail reports.
episodes.157824: A mid-level shortwave trough crossed the Mid-Atlantic region on June 14, 2021, generating a line of storms that developed over northwestern Pennsylvania by late morning and progressed east-southeastward through the afternoon hours. Sporadic wind damage was observed with this line, with most of this occurring within a single, long-lived bowing segment that progressed from Elk County east-southeastward along the I-80 corridor to Columbia County.
episodes.157847: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the mid-afternoon hours across Northcentral Louisiana on June 13th, near a weak surface trough extending from Southeast Oklahoma, extreme Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana. Compressional warming and low level moisture pooling near this boundary resulted in a very unstable air mass developing across much of the region, with a weak upper level disturbance sliding southwest across North Louisiana and East Texas during the afternoon and evening contributing to increasing large scale ascent. These storms continued to redevelop and shift west-southwest across North Louisiana through the evening and into East Texas after midnight. Some of these storms re-intensified and became severe over Harrison and Upshur Counties, with trees downed east of Hallsville and quarter size hail falling in Gilmer. These storms finally diminished between 3-4 am on the 14th.
episodes.157887: A cold front and associated weak area of surface low pressure approached the mid-Atlantic on June 14. A seasonably warm air mass was present ahead of the front, allowing a moderate amount of instability to build over the mid-Atlantic. Moderate to strong wind shear was also present thanks to the presence of a robust upper level disturbance approaching the region. This disturbance, along with the front, provided sufficient forcing for scattered to widespread convection to develop in the interior mid-Atlantic and propagate towards the coast. Some storms became strong to severe in the rather favorable convective environment, posing a primary risk of damaging winds along with some hail. Convection also continued well into the overnight over portions of the area thanks to the good shear and forcing, with convection eventually moving offshore in the pre-dawn hours of the 15th.

Ahead of this front, a warm and moist airmass provided the perfect environment for thunderstorms to develop. These thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and small hail, with numerous reports of trees being blown down as they rolled through.
episodes.157942: Numerous afternoon thunderstorms that pushed offshore along the coast in Brevard and Indian River counties produced strong wind gusts.

episodes.158247: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the evening hours across north-central, northeast, and east-central Wisconsin.  The strongest storms produced isolated wind damage and small hail.
episodes.158249: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front across northeast Wisconsin.  Strong storms produced gusty winds as they tracked over Lake Michigan during the evening hours. Thunderstorm winds capsized a boat on the southern Bay of Green Bay, causing a fatality.

episodes.158784: Several impulses embedded within a positively tilted mid-level trough across the region worked in concert with sufficient moisture to produce widespread thunderstorms across South Florida. A few storms resulted in damaging wind gusts across Broward County.
episodes.158785: Several impulses embedded within a positively tilted mid-level trough across the region worked in concert with sufficient moisture to produce widespread thunderstorms across South Florida. A few storms resulted in strong wind gusts across the Atlantic Waters.
episodes.158814: A stationary front meandered near the FL-GA state line under a mean layer upper level trough across the eastern U.S. Diurnal instability combined with the sea breezes, outflows, upper level energy and high moisture all under weak steering flow produced locally heavy rainfall and isolated pulse severe storms.
episodes.158942: Severe storms developed along an approaching front on Monday, June 14th. Strong shear (60kts in the 0-6km layer), moderate instability (CAPE of 1000-1500 J/kg), and dry mid-level air helped produce strong downdrafts and hail.
episodes.158943: Severe storms developed along an approaching front on Monday, June 14th. Strong shear (60kts in the 0-6km layer), moderate instability (CAPE of 1000-1500 J/kg), and dry mid-level air helped produce strong downdrafts and hail.

episodes.159036: A cold front combined with an unstable atmosphere, plenty of moisture, and a light flow aloft to cause isolated flooding instances over the Potomac Highlands of Virginia as well as central Virginia.

episodes.159134: A surface trough passed through Central New York, triggering scattered severe thunderstorms along the boundary. The winds associated with these storms blew down trees, snapped utility poles, and blew a roof off of a trailer.
episodes.159152: An upper level disturbance swept through the Ohio Valley on June 14th with showers and thunderstorms aligned along a surface cold front. Several thunderstorms became severe that evening which resulted in downed trees and power lines due to damaging wind gusts. Rain from the previous day's severe weather primed the area for flash flooding and heavy downpours on the 14th ultimately resulted in high water issues in the Buckhannon area.
episodes.159177: A strong cold front in accordance with a passing low pressure system pressed into West Virginia on the evening of June 13th. Strong to severe thunderstorms accompanied the front, resulting in multiple instances of downed trees and power lines due to damaging wind gusts. Due to the combination of heavy downpours and multiple storms passing over the area that day, several counties observed flash flooding. The most notable events occurred in Gilmer County, where a large shed on a golf course was swept away by the rushing high water, and Pocahontas County, where a swift water rescue was conducted in the town of Frost.
episodes.159221: A cold front sweeping through the area on the evening of June 13th resulted in a severe thunderstorm to transpire in Buchanan County. Damaging wind gusts with this storm caused a tree to fall near the town of Grundy, which resulted in one injury.
episodes.159311: A persistent upper-level trough over the eastern U.S. and a cold front dropping south through the state brought scattered strong and isolated severe thunderstorms to north and central Georgia.
episodes.159313: Thunderstorms developed along an outflow boundary east of South Central Texas. This line of storms moved to the west into a hot airmass. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.159493: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail across parts of Adams, Arapahoe, Denver, and Weld counties.  The hail ranged in size from quarter to golfball size.  The hail did cause some damage to vehicles at Cherry Creek State Park.  Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 59 mph were observed in Morgan and Logan counties.
episodes.159504: Unstable conditions were present during the afternoon when an upper level trough moved across Northeastern Pennsylvania. Isolated storms formed along the boundary, with a few becoming severe. These severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds, knocking down trees and utility wires.
episodes.159584: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon hours of Monday, June 14, 2021. Severe hail was observed across portions of Herkimer and Schoharie counties with the largest hailstones estimated to be about the size of golf balls.
episodes.159647: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 13th, with a few severe wind reports received.
episodes.159816: Slow-moving thunderstorms trained across southern Highland County, forming in an environment of CAPE exceeding 2,500 J/Kg and Precipitable Water of around 1.5 inches.  The storms produced 2.5 to 4 inches of rainfall amounts over a 2 to 3-hour period, with rainfall rates at times reaching 5 to 6 inches per hour.  Steep terrain in the Back Creek basin aided in creating efficient runoff to cause the stream gauge at Back Creek at Sunrise to rise to 10.01 feet, exceeding Moderate Flood Stage set at 10 feet.  This is the highest this gauge has risen since 2008.  FLASH estimated that rainfall just upstream from the stream gauge was over 3 times greater than 1-hour Flash Flood Guidance.  CREST Unit Streamflow was estimating over 1,000 cfs per square mile, whiile CREST 1-hour Average Return Interval estimates put this rainfall at well over a 200-year event.
episodes.159835: A narrow corridor of elevated instability around 1000 J/kg combined with effective shear of 30-35 knots in the exit region of the low-level jet to produce scattered thunderstorms overnight.  A few briefly stronger updrafts produced hail, with isolated reports up to quarter size.
episodes.159842: A couple rounds of thunderstorms developed in central and north central South Dakota, one around noon and another around midnight, and produced severe wind and hail.
episodes.159877: An afternoon thunderstorm produced quarter sized hail in Hamilton County.
episodes.159952: Thunderstorms developed in the northern Nebraska Panhandle in the vicinity of a weak surface boundary. As storms drifted east, they became severe across the northwestern Sandhills and the northeastern Nebraska Panhandle. Hail up to ping pong ball size was reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.160076: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed around the I-25 corridor on this day, given a more favorable setup in this location. While the storms were primarily limited to this location, several severe storms producing large hail did occur across the Pikes Peak region during the evening hours.
episodes.160115: Scattered thunderstorms developed across upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. A couple of the storms produced large hail.
episodes.160116: Isolated thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced large hail in Catawba County.
episodes.160151: A weak boundary moved into southeast Texas during the morning of the 14th. Storms formed along this boundary and moved southwest along the Texas coast. The storms moved into a region of higher instability in the afternoon over the Middle Texas coast. The storms produced wind damage from Victoria and Port Lavaca southwest to Beeville and|Lake Corpus Christi. Wind gusts from 60 to 70 mph blew trees and power poles down, broke tree limbs, and caused roof damage.
episodes.160152: Storms formed along an outflow boundary along the Middle Texas coast during the afternoon. Wind gusts from 40 to 50 knots occurred with these storms around Port Lavaca.
episodes.160299: Strong instability resulted in isolated to scattered thunderstorms. A few storms were severe and produced mainly wind damage.

Several significant events of wind damage occurred as these storms spread across the region, with some houses impacted by high wind and fallen trees.
